info.title: AV Scenario Stress-Tester API
info.description:
Read-only access to the AV scenario stress-tester's results.

Scenarios are ranked by **fragility score** (higher = closer to catastrophe), and
each one can be inspected: its danger metrics, the minimum perturbation that causes
a collision, and the agent trajectories to draw it.

**Coordinates are local planar metres, not longitude/latitude.** Waymo Open Motion
Dataset scenarios use a local metric frame; treating these values as lon/lat will
place every scenario off the coast of West Africa and make every distance
meaningless.

Nothing here starts a computation — the optimizer runs offline and this API reads
what it wrote.

get.description:
Liveness check that actually touches the database.

A health check that only returns {"status": "ok"} without querying will report
healthy while the database is unreachable — which is the exact failure it
exists to catch. So this executes a real round-trip.

The status says what the round-trips found. "ok": the database answered and so
did PostGIS (its version is in `postgis`). "degraded": the database answered but
PostGIS did not, because the extension is missing or the call raised; `postgis`
is then null. The scores endpoints do not use PostGIS and keep working; the
geometry endpoints do use it. A degraded answer is still HTTP 200, on purpose:
the hosting platform's health check reads this route and takes an instance out
of rotation on any 4xx or 5xx, which would also take down the endpoints that
still work. A database that cannot be reached is a failure of the connection
dependency, not a status here: a 503 with Retry-After when the pool is exhausted.

Corpus-level counts for the dashboard header.

`count(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)` computes every count in ONE pass over the table,
rather than issuing nine separate COUNT queries that each scan it again.

The ranked list, most fragile first, keyset-paginated.

ORDERING
--------
The API orders by `fragility_score DESC, scenario_id`: the same two keys, in the
same directions, as ranker.rank_scenarios' sort key
`(-fragility_score, str(scenario_id))`. The intent is deliberate: if the API and
the batch pipeline ordered differently, "rank 3" would mean two different
scenarios depending on who you asked.

WHAT IS GUARANTEED, AND WHAT DEPENDS ON THE DATABASE. Rows with DIFFERENT scores
come out in the same order from both. Rows that TIE are ordered by scenario_id,
and there the two sides use different comparators: PostgreSQL sorts the TEXT
column by the database's collation, Python sorts `str` by code point. They agree
for the ids in the tests (lowercase ASCII, such as `syn_medium_a` before
`syn_medium_b`) and under the C collation. They can disagree under a locale
collation, for example for ids that differ in case or punctuation. This
repository does not record which collation the hosted database uses, and the
check in tests/test_api.py that the API order equals rank_scenarios' order uses
only lowercase ASCII ids, so it cannot tell the two apart. "Byte-identical" holds
only under the C collation; do not rely on it for other ids.

PAGINATION DOES NOT DEPEND ON THAT. The ORDER BY and the cursor predicate below
compare scenario_id as the same column under the same collation, so, while the
table does not change between requests, every row is served exactly once, in a
stable order, whichever collation is in use. Only agreement with the batch
ranker's order among tied rows is conditional.

The scenario_id tiebreak is LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic. Without a unique second
key, rows tied on fragility_score have no defined order, and the same row can
be served on two consecutive pages (or skipped entirely) as the database
happens to return ties differently between queries.

WHY KEYSET AND NOT LIMIT/OFFSET
-------------------------------
OFFSET is not just slow, it is WRONG under concurrent writes: if a row is
inserted above the current position between two requests, every subsequent row
shifts down by one, and the client silently sees a duplicate at the page
boundary (or, on delete, a gap). Keyset pagination anchors on a value rather
than a count: the cursor holds the score and id of the last row served, and the
next page is the rows strictly after that position in the ordering. So inserting
or deleting OTHER rows does not move the boundary, and the rows still to come are
not repeated or skipped because of it. That is all it guarantees. Each request is
a separate query with no shared snapshot: a row inserted or deleted behind the
cursor is simply not seen by the later pages, and a row whose fragility_score
changes between two requests can cross the boundary and be skipped or served
twice. That stability against inserts and deletes is why this is here.

WHAT THIS QUERY COSTS — AND WHY IT IS NOT A SEEK
------------------------------------------------
PostgreSQL compiles a ROW COMPARISON, `(a, b) < (c, d)`, into an Index Cond —
a genuine seek straight to the cursor position. But a row comparison is only
VALID when every column sorts the same direction, because it is lexicographic
in one direction by definition. Our ordering is mixed — fragility_score DESC,
scenario_id ASC — so the correct predicate after a cursor (f0, s0) is:

    f < f0  OR  (f = f0 AND s > s0)

and an OR-form predicate is NOT recognized as an index condition. It becomes a
Filter: the scan starts at the top of the index and discards every row before
the cursor. Measured on a 50k-row table with the composite index present:

    tuple form (f, s) < (f0, s0)   Index Only Scan + Index Cond   0.03 ms
    OR form (what we use)          Index Only Scan + Filter       8.68 ms
                                   (25005 rows removed by filter)

So: we keep keyset pagination's CORRECTNESS property (stable page boundaries,
no duplicates, no gaps) and give up its PERFORMANCE property — page N again
costs proportional to N, the same asymptotics as OFFSET. Do not describe this
query as a seek.

Both properties are recoverable by ordering `fragility_score DESC, scenario_id
DESC` and using the tuple form, which in ranker.py is
`sorted(records, key=lambda r: (r['fragility_score'], r['scenario_id']),
reverse=True)` — same direction on both columns. That is the escape hatch if
deep paging ever becomes real. It is not taken here because it would change
Phase 5 code to buy nothing at this scale: a shard holds a few hundred
scenarios, and the dashboard will never page deep enough for a filter over a
few thousand rows to be noticeable. Matching the ranker's ordering is worth
more than the seek today.

The composite index (fragility_score DESC, scenario_id), created in
export_geometry.GEOMETRY_SCHEMA_SQL, still earns its keep: it serves the
ORDER BY, so this is an Index Only Scan rather than a sort.
One scenario's full row, including the raw perturbation vector.

The most recent runs of the offline pipeline, newest first, as their manifests recorded them.

Only the public columns (the view pipeline_runs_public); `package_versions`, `parameters` and `counts` through allow-lists. An
empty list when no run is recorded or the manifest tables are not in this database: both are normal states.

schema.title: Response List Pipeline Runs Pipeline Runs Get

get.description:
Where this scenario's stored result came from: the run id, the scene fingerprint, which agent is the SDC, when it was
scored and searched, and how it was searched (the public keys of the stored search provenance).

404 ONLY when the scenario is unknown. A scenario with no stored search returns 200 with nulls: "nothing recorded" is a
normal state. Read from `scenario_scores` alone; the stored blob is served through an allow-list (src/api/provenance.py),
never whole, and a value of the wrong type is null rather than an error.

How the stored search closed in on its answer, from a recorded re-run of it (src/scoring/search_runs.py).

A trace is served only if a re-run is recorded that names THIS stored result (`reruns_stress_run_id` = the stored `stress_run_id`),
searched the same scene, and ended within src/api/trace.py TRACE_DELTA_TOLERANCE of the stored delta (the query applies it, so a newer
re-run that ended elsewhere does not hide an older one that followed the stored search; a difference that is NULL or NaN is not below
anything). Otherwise 200 with `trace` null: "no trace" is a normal state. 404 only when the scenario is unknown. When several re-runs
qualify, the newest is served.

Every agent's logged path for one scenario.

404 only when the scenario itself is unknown — checked against scenario_scores,
because "this scenario exists but its geometry has not been exported yet" is a
normal state that must not look like a missing scenario. That case returns 200
with an empty agents list.

ST_AsGeoJSON does the geometry-to-JSON conversion inside PostgreSQL: less data
on the wire than WKT, no geometry library needed in the API process, and the
result drops straight into a deck.gl PathLayer.

BUT GeoJSON has no M dimension, and ST_AsGeoJSON silently DROPS it —
`LINESTRING M(1 2 0, 3 4 1)` comes back as `[[1,2],[3,4]]` with the measures
gone. Since M is what tells the frontend which timestep each vertex belongs to,
it is fetched alongside with ST_DumpPoints + ST_M, ordered by vertex position
so it stays index-aligned with the coordinates.

The challenger's logged path next to its minimally-perturbed one — the Phase 4
result, made drawable.

404 ONLY when the scenario is unknown. A scenario that exists but has not been
stress-tested returns 200 with null paths: "nothing to show yet" is a normal
state in a pipeline whose expensive pass runs over a chosen subset, and a
frontend should render an empty panel for it, not an error.

AgentTrack.title: AgentTrack
AgentTrack.description:
One agent's path through space and time.

`path`, `timesteps` and `headings` are index-aligned: element i of each
describes the same vertex. Coordinates are LOCAL PLANAR METRES, not lon/lat.

`lengths_m` and `widths_m` are index-aligned with them too: element i is the
agent's box size at vertex i, which is the size the collision check used at that
frame. A null ELEMENT means the recorded size at that frame was unusable (not
finite, or not above zero). A null ARRAY means this agent was exported before
per-frame sizes were recorded, or the database has no such columns; `length_m` and
`width_m` (read at the first valid frame) are all there is then. The scalars are
unchanged and remain what they were.

ttc_none.title: Ttc None
ttc_none.description: min_ttc is the 999.0 sentinel: the SDC is never in a closing pair; the term is 0.

pet_none.title: Pet None
pet_none.description: min_pet is the 999.0 sentinel: no shared conflict zone; the term is 0.

ttc_at_floor.title: Ttc At Floor
ttc_at_floor.description: min_ttc is at or below the floor, so its signal is capped.

pet_at_floor.title: Pet At Floor
pet_at_floor.description: min_pet is at or below the floor (an overlap included), so its signal is capped.

FragilityBreakdown.title: FragilityBreakdown
FragilityBreakdown.description:
The two terms of the stored `fragility_score`, worked out from the stored `min_ttc` and `min_pet`.

The score ranks the recorded scene only (no perturbation term):

    fragility = ttc_weight * ttc_signal + pet_weight * pet_signal

with `ttc_weight` 0.4/0.7 and `pet_weight` 0.3/0.7, and each signal 1 / max(value, floor), or 0 when the value is the 999.0
"none" sentinel. The floors are 0.01 s: a value at or below the floor, a PET of zero or an overlap (negative PET)
included, contributes the same as 0.01 s. `reproduces_stored_score` says whether the two terms add up to the stored score;
when it is false the breakdown does not describe that score and is not to be shown as if it did.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description:
Liveness plus a real database round-trip.

`status` is "ok" when the database and PostGIS both answered, and "degraded" when the
database answered but PostGIS did not: `postgis` is then None (the extension is
missing, or the version call raised). That is degraded, not dead: the scores
endpoints work fine without it, only geometry is unavailable. Both are HTTP 200.

PackageVersions.title: PackageVersions
PackageVersions.description: The versions the run recorded: Python and the five packages the pipeline depends on. Null = not recorded.

PerturbedResponse.title: PerturbedResponse
PerturbedResponse.description:
The Phase 4 answer, made drawable: the challenger's logged path next to its
minimally-perturbed one.

Every field except scenario_id is nullable, because "this scenario has not been
stress-tested yet" is a normal state that returns 200, not an error.

delta_labels USED to be the second exception, and this docstring said so. It stopped
being one in Batch 3 (audit B13): a delta can only be labelled if we know which
kinematic model produced it, and for a legacy row with neither recorded provenance
nor exported geometry, nothing does. Corrected here rather than quietly reworded,
because the old sentence is exactly the guarantee a frontend would have been written
against.

PipelineRun.title: PipelineRun
PipelineRun.description:
One run of the offline pipeline, as its manifest recorded it (the public columns only: the command line, the host label and the
notes are never served).

Every text column is checked before it is served (src/api/manifest.py): `kind` and `status` must be one of the known words, the revision 40 hex
digits, the checksum 64, the Python version a version string and `shard_name` a file name (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, at most 200
characters); anything else is null, not repaired. Null always means "not recorded for this run", never "none". `git_dirty` true means the working tree had uncommitted changes when
the run started, so the revision alone does not reproduce the code. `package_versions`, `parameters` and `counts` are served through
allow-lists of keys and types (src/api/manifest.py); a key that is not listed is not served, and a value of the wrong type is null.
The times are those of the run, in UTC.

run.description: The manifest of the run that stored this result, found through pipeline_run_results by scenario and stress_run_id (the most recent if several are linked). Null when no manifest is recorded for this result: the results stored before manifests existed have none, and that is not an error.

delta_labels.title: Delta Labels
delta_labels.description: The names, with units, of the components of the perturbation under the parameterization recorded in `search`, from the table GET /perturbed uses (DELTA_LABELS_BY_PARAMETERIZATION). Null when no parameterization is recorded or it is one this API does not know. A client names `search.bounds` with them only when the labels GET /perturbed served are the same list.

ProvenanceResponse.title: ProvenanceResponse
ProvenanceResponse.description:
Where a scenario's stored result came from, for the reader who wants to check it or reproduce it.

Read from `scenario_scores` only. Every field is null when it was not recorded; a scenario with no stored search has
nulls and `search` null. `stress_run_id` is the hash of the run's identity (the inputs it was searched with and the
code-contract versions), `scene_fingerprint` the hash of the scene it was searched against, `sdc_idx` which agent was the
SDC. The times are when the scenario was scored, when a stress-test pass last reached it, and when the stored result was
written; they are timestamps of the offline runs, in UTC, not of any request to this API.

RunCounts.title: RunCounts
RunCounts.description: What the run reported having done. Null = not reported, never zero.

RunParameters.title: RunParameters
RunParameters.description: The parameters that varied a run: seeds, budgets, the number of challengers. Null = not reported.

min_ttc.title: Min Ttc
min_ttc.description: Minimum time-to-collision (s) over pairs involving the SDC. 999.0 sentinel = the SDC is never in a closing pair.

min_pet.title: Min Pet
min_pet.description: Minimum post-encroachment time (s) over pairs involving the SDC. Negative = the SDC and another agent genuinely occupied a conflict zone simultaneously. 999.0 = no shared conflict zone.

baseline_offset_at_collision.title: Baseline Offset At Collision
baseline_offset_at_collision.description: Distance in metres, at the collision frame, between the zero-perturbation replay of the challenger and its logged position. Null when no collision was found or the figure was not recorded for the stored result. Not comparable with min_perturbation, a weighted norm over components of mixed units.

baseline_replay_error.title: Baseline Replay Error
baseline_replay_error.description: Largest distance in metres, over the whole track, between the zero-perturbation replay of the challenger and its logged position. Null when the figure was not recorded for the stored result. Not comparable with min_perturbation, a weighted norm over components of mixed units.

ScenarioDetail.title: ScenarioDetail
ScenarioDetail.description: A single scenario, including the raw perturbation vector.

ScenarioPage.title: ScenarioPage
ScenarioPage.description:
One page of the ranked list.

`next_cursor` is opaque: clients pass it back verbatim and must never construct
or edit one. See routes.py for why its precision is load-bearing.

min_ttc.title: Min Ttc
min_ttc.description: Minimum time-to-collision (s) over pairs involving the SDC. 999.0 sentinel = the SDC is never in a closing pair.

min_pet.title: Min Pet
min_pet.description: Minimum post-encroachment time (s) over pairs involving the SDC. Negative = the SDC and another agent genuinely occupied a conflict zone simultaneously. 999.0 = no shared conflict zone.

ScenarioSummary.title: ScenarioSummary
ScenarioSummary.description: One row of the ranked list.

delta_parameterization.title: Delta Parameterization
delta_parameterization.description: 'bicycle' or 'linear': which model's units the four components of the delta carry.

selected_stage.title: Selected Stage
selected_stage.description: Which stage's answer the stored result is: 'de' or 'de+autograd'.

SearchRecord.title: SearchRecord
SearchRecord.description:
How the stored result was searched: the keys of `search_provenance` that are public, each as recorded or null.

Null means "not recorded for this result" (an older result, or a key the search did not write) and is never zero. The keys
are an allow-list (src/api/provenance.py); nothing else in the stored blob is served. `bounds` has one [low, high] per
component of the perturbation, in the order of `delta` and `delta_labels`.

StatsResponse.title: StatsResponse
StatsResponse.description: Corpus-level summary for the dashboard header.

generation.title: Generation
generation.description: 1 for the first generation of Differential Evolution that the search completed.

n_eval_cumulative.title: N Eval Cumulative
n_eval_cumulative.description: How many candidates had been evaluated when this generation ended.

best_weighted_norm.title: Best Weighted Norm
best_weighted_norm.description: The smallest weighted norm of a candidate that exactly collides, among all evaluated so far. Null until one has been found.

max_abs_delta_difference.title: Max Abs Delta Difference
max_abs_delta_difference.description: How far the re-run's final delta is from the stored delta (largest absolute difference of any component). Null when no trace is served.

tolerance.title: Tolerance
tolerance.description: The largest difference at which a trace is served.

TraceResponse.title: TraceResponse
TraceResponse.description:
How a stored search closed in on its answer: the best weighted norm found after each generation of Differential Evolution.

The trace belongs to a RE-RUN of the stored search (same seed and budget, with a callback that only records), not to the stored
run itself, and it is served only when that re-run ended at the stored delta to within `tolerance` (the largest absolute difference
in any component). `trace` is null when no trace is recorded for this result, when the recorded re-run ended somewhere else, or when
the result it re-ran is not the one now stored: all normal states. The trace covers the Differential Evolution stage only; when the
stored result was then refined by gradient descent, its norm can be lower than the trace's last point.

TrajectoryResponse.title: TrajectoryResponse
TrajectoryResponse.description: Every agent's logged path for one scenario. Empty if Pass 3 has not run.
